events.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) back to a limited practice Friday after sitting Thursday; Monday at Chicago in question
events.detail: Smith missed Thursday practice with a hamstring injury and returned as a limited participant Friday, stretching without a jersey. The Eagles play Monday night at Chicago, so Saturday practice and the Saturday report decide his designation. Tight end Dallas Goedert is already out with an MCL sprain.
events.so_what: Monday-night hamstrings are the lineup trap of the week: if Smith is a late scratch, most managers have no Monday replacement left. Line up a Sunday-afternoon alternative before Sunday games lock, or accept the risk. With Goedert out, a healthy Smith has fewer mouths competing for Hurts targets.

events.headline: Michael Pittman questionable vs. Bengals after limited practices all week with a new foot injury
events.detail: Pittman was limited Wednesday through Friday with a foot injury, separate from his training-camp issue, that kept him out of Week 2. He carries a Questionable tag for Sunday against Cincinnati; Germie Bernard filled the role in Week 2. Rico Dowdle is already out for Pittsburgh.
events.so_what: Three limited sessions is the optimistic side of questionable, but he missed last week with the same foot, so confirm he is active before the early-afternoon lock. If he sits, Bernard is a one-week desperation FLEX at best, not a waiver priority.

events.headline: Commanders rule out surgery for Jayden Daniels; week-to-week in a brace, Week 4 in London the next checkpoint
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. After specialist visits in New York and Los Angeles, GM Adam Peters said surgery is not on the table and IR has not been discussed. Daniels is week-to-week and will play in an elbow brace when he returns; the team's reported window is within about four weeks, with the first real decision before Week 4 against the Colts in London. Marcus Mariota starts Week 3 against Seattle.
events.so_what: The season-ending outcome is off the table, which is the big change: Daniels is a hold, not a drop. He still misses Week 3 and probably more, so a roster leaning on him needs a quarterback for the next two to four weeks. When he is back, a braced non-throwing elbow is the thing to watch for whether he keeps running, since the rushing yards are most of his konami-premium value.

league_notes.pit: Daniels is WreckingCrew09's.
league_notes.clash: Daniels is ChrisHasAfib's.

events.headline: Mike Evans questionable vs. Cardinals after returning to practice Friday with the hip injury
events.detail: Evans hurt his hip in the second half of the Week 2 win over Miami and missed Wednesday and Thursday practice while Kyle Shanahan said the injury would 'have to be managed.' He was back on the field Friday and carries a Questionable designation into Sunday's home game against Arizona. Ian Rapoport earlier described the injury as not major. The 49ers are already without Demarcus Robinson (high ankle sprain, Out).
events.so_what: A Friday return after two missed days reads as a player who is going to dress, but Questionable is still a forecast, so check the inactive list before a Sunday afternoon kickoff. With Robinson out, the 49ers are thin enough at receiver that Evans should see a full route share if he goes, which keeps his touchdown equity in the red zone intact.

events.headline: Jaylen Wright doubtful vs. Chiefs with a stinger and foot injury; Ollie Gordon backs up Achane
events.detail: Wright was limited Wednesday and Thursday, did not practice Friday, and is listed Doubtful for Sunday at Kansas City after the stinger he suffered in the Week 2 loss to San Francisco plus a foot issue. De'Von Achane has played 83 percent of Miami's offensive snaps through two weeks; Ollie Gordon is the favorite for whatever work Achane leaves, with Carlos Washington Jr. or Jarquez Hunter a possible practice-squad elevation.
events.so_what: Wright was a backup behind a back on the field for 83 percent of snaps, so nothing much changes for Achane, who stays a locked-in start. Gordon picks up the short-yardage and change-of-pace work, which in this format means a touchdown-dependent dart, not a flex.

events.headline: Caleb Williams unlikely to play Monday vs. Eagles, per Rapoport; Case Keenum set to start
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 24 item. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports Williams is unlikely to play Monday night against Philadelphia with the hamstring strain he suffered on a fourth-quarter scramble against Minnesota (MRI showed no tear). Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol after a hit from Andrew Van Ginkel, and both were non-participants Thursday, so 38-year-old Case Keenum is in line for his first regular-season start since 2023. Kyle Monangai (knee) and kicker Cairo Santos (right hip) were also Thursday non-participants. Hamstrings like Williams's typically cost two to four weeks.
events.so_what: Plan the Monday game around Keenum rather than hoping for a late Williams surprise, and treat every Bears pass catcher as a downgrade. Monangai's knee still matters: if he sits, D'Andre Swift's share of the backfield grows. Santos's hip keeps the Bears kicker in doubt, and a kicker who might not dress can't be trusted to score by the distance bands.

events.headline: Sam Darnold cleared, no designation; he starts Sunday at Washington
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Darnold (glute) practiced fully Thursday and Friday and is off Seattle's final injury report; Mike Macdonald called him ready to play, so he takes the job back from Drew Lock. RB Jadarian Price (chest) also practiced fully and carries no designation. Washington is without Jayden Daniels, so Marcus Mariota starts for the Commanders.
events.so_what: Darnold is a usable QB start again and Lock goes back to the bench, so drop him if you streamed him. A Seattle offense with its starter back also firms up its pass catchers.

Travis Homer and rookie Eli Heidenreich back him up.
events.so_what: Start Warren as an RB2 if he is active; his Sunday status is the only open question, and the gameday routine covers inactives. Homer is the handcuff only if Warren is a surprise scratch. Bench Dowdle.

events.headline: Jaxson Dart undergoes season-ending knee surgery; Jameis Winston is the Giants starter
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. Dart had season-ending surgery Wednesday and the Giants formally placed him on injured reserve Thursday; the damage includes the MCL, PCL and meniscus, with no ACL involvement. Jameis Winston was already named the starter going forward, beginning Week 3 at home against Tennessee. Malik Nabers' right shoulder popped out in the same Monday night loss to the Rams; he popped it back in and returned, and no further diagnosis has been reported. On Wednesday the Giants listed Nabers as limited with the shoulder (an estimated report, since they held a walkthrough), with no quotes on his status.
events.so_what: No longer a planning question: Dart is done for 2026 and the Giants' rushing-QB premium goes with him. Winston throws more and riskier balls, which can mean more volume for Nabers and the other pass catchers alongside more drive-ending interceptions (only a point each here). Nabers being limited rather than out on the first report is a mild positive; watch Friday's designation before locking him in.

events.headline: Falcons rout Packers 35-14 on TNF: Penix active and efficient, Bijan runs for 194, Packers' backfield manages 17 yards
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. Michael Penix Jr. was active after a full practice and went 18 of 25 for 256 yards, a touchdown and an interception in his first start back from the ACL. Atlanta ran for 244 yards: Bijan Robinson had 194 and a touchdown, Brian Robinson Jr. added a score, and Drake London caught 9 passes for 194 yards. Green Bay ran only nine times for 17 yards, with MarShawn Lloyd (4-11) and Kaleb Johnson (4-6) splitting the carries; Josh Jacobs remains on the commissioner exempt list and Jayden Reed was out. Jordan Love threw 52 times for 312 yards and two touchdowns.
events.so_what: Penix running an offense this efficiently keeps Bijan and London at the top of their positions rather than capped behind a struggling quarterback. The Packers have no running game: neither Lloyd nor Kaleb Johnson is a start while the carries are split this way at this volume, and a Love who throws 52 times is a volume play, not a fade.

events.headline: Saints' backfield confirmed a three-man committee: Etienne led in snaps (37) over Kamara (20) and CJ Donaldson (20)
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 20 item. A fuller snap-count picture from Kamara's return game shows Etienne with the most offensive snaps at 37, with Kamara and CJ Donaldson each at 20. Kamara still led all three in touches (14) with the receiving-down role, while Etienne's edge is more early-down and Donaldson took goal-line-adjacent work. Kellen Moore has framed the workload as matchup-dependent rather than a fixed order.
events.so_what: This is a real three-way split, not a two-man competition with a clear leader — Etienne's snap lead does not translate to a touch lead, and Donaldson's role means neither Kamara nor Etienne is a safe bell-cow bet even in a flex-friendly 2-FLEX format. Hold all three and let more weeks of data settle it before trading from either side.
